clue.text: Contract debts without interest

parts.note: to contract a debt or illness is to incur it
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Someone takes on debts that carry no interest charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incurious lacks curiosity, showing no interest in things around them.

clue.text: Suggest I am to practise a trade

parts.note: I am contracts to I'M
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Someone hints that they intend to take up a trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to suggest it without stating it outright.

clue.text: Last drop of drama

parts.note: reads like the final dribble of something theatrical, but means the fabric that falls at the end of a play

explanation.surface: The final dribble of something theatrical.
explanation.definitionFit: At the end of a stage performance the stage cloth is lowered, the final drop.

clue.text: A trio's broken relationship

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces and can be put back together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A group of three has had its relationship fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the quantitative relationship between two amounts.

clue.text: Unusual when Bobby isn't on his round

definitions.meaning: a British policeman (a bobby) not on his patrol route is literally away from his beat

explanation.surface: It's strange when the local policeman isn't walking his patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOBBY is British slang for a police officer, and his BEAT is the route he patrols.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat describes something unconventional or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Counterpart of a papal bull that's above criticism?

definitions.text: Counterpart of a papal bull that's above criticism?

parts.words: Counterpart of a papal bull that's above criticism?
parts.note: a papal bull is a decree, but read as a holy male bovine its female counterpart would be a holy cow, and such a thing is proverbially beyond reproach

explanation.surface: Asks what corresponds to an unchallengeable decree from the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an institution or belief held to be beyond question or criticism.

clue.text: Cries of ravens or motherless parrots

indicators.note: losing mother means the word for mother is taken away

parts.note: macaws are large tropical parrots

explanation.surface: Contrasts the cries of ravens with parrots that have lost their mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Caw is the harsh call made by crows and ravens.

clue.text: Trying only made things worse for him

definitions.text: Trying only made things worse for him

parts.words: Trying only made things worse for him
parts.note: trying sounds like making an effort, but here it means being tried in a court, after which this man was found guilty

explanation.surface: Someone whose efforts only made matters worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A person found guilty after a trial in court is a convicted criminal.

clue.text: Drudge has artist's creation to mount

parts.note: an artist's creation is a work of art
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A labourer gets a painting of a horse to put up.
explanation.definitionFit: A workhorse is someone who does hard, dull work reliably, a drudge.

clue.text: Suitable anger with which father sent back the drink

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so these words are read from end to start

parts.note: fit means suitable
ire is anger
PA is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: An angry father returns a drink as unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the whole run FITIREPA end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Recent change of heart

indicators.note: a change of these letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has lately had a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' looks like a set phrase; the definition is just 'heart'.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its middle or core.

clue.text: Current supplier has Monday off

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or being out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electricity company has taken Monday off.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator that produces electric current.

clue.text: Pupil power I mention in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the words are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: taken as written, a letter said aloud; to mention is to cite

explanation.surface: A speaker refers to the power of school pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: The pupil is part of the eye, and its power is the faculty of vision.

clue.text: Puts out of sight

parts.note: can mean hides something away, or deprives someone of vision, or describes window screens that conceal a room

explanation.surface: Someone hides things away.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive of vision; also window screens that conceal the view.

clue.text: Car minus oil — engine head exploded

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart and its pieces land in a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A car without oil suffers an engine explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes E from 'engine' to join MINUSOIL before 'exploded' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious car, often chauffeur-driven.

clue.text: Calm the good man with a complaint

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a good man
a complaint can be an ailment or illness

explanation.surface: A good man stays calm despite his ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stillness is a state of quiet and calm, without motion.

clue.text: Understood vessel can be reserved

parts.note: tacit means understood without being stated
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A container may be booked once it is agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means habitually quiet and uncommunicative, reserved in manner.

clue.text: This arm's moved quickly

indicators.note: moved suggests the letters are shifted into new positions

explanation.surface: Someone notes their arm moved fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartish is informal British for quickly or promptly.

clue.text: Time for students to collect together

definitions.text: Time for students to collect together

parts.words: Time for students to collect together
parts.note: reads like a period for students to gather, but means a week when British students collect money for charity with stunts

explanation.surface: A period when students gather as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, students' RAG events are charity fundraising stunts and collections.
explanation.definitionFit: A British university week of charity fundraising events and street collections by students.

clue.text: We linger outside, nevertheless

indicators.note: the word for linger stays outside the other piece, wrapping it

parts.note: to hover is to linger close by
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group stays outside in spite of something.
explanation.definitionFit: However and nevertheless both introduce a contrasting statement.

clue.text: Note carrier soaked and all in

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: soaked means wet

explanation.surface: Someone's wallet got wet and they are exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a pocket case for carrying banknotes.

clue.text: Rock singer learning what Romanians use for money

parts.note: lore is learning or traditional knowledge
the leu is Romania's currency, plural lei

explanation.surface: A rock vocalist learns about Romanian money.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine, and in legend the siren whose singing lured boatmen to their doom.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend a siren sat on a Rhine cliff, singing sailors to destruction.

clue.text: Stop in front of a humble building

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the following ones

parts.note: a bung is a stopper
low means humble or lowly

explanation.surface: Someone halts before a modest building.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey house, a type of building.

clue.text: Staff taken in by salary — it's a travesty

indicators.note: taken in by means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: salary is pay
a rod is a staff

explanation.surface: Staff paid by salary call it a travesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody is a mocking imitation, which can be a travesty of the original.

clue.text: Copper band?

parts.note: looks like a ring of copper metal, but copper is slang for a police officer, so a band of them

explanation.surface: Asks about a ring made of copper.
explanation.walkthrough: COPPER is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a body of men summoned by a sheriff to help enforce law.

clue.text: Needs to be close

indicators.note: to be suggests the letters must become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Something must be close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense means thick and closely packed together.

clue.text: No tricks, that's a promise

parts.note: sounds like a pledge of honesty, but is a card bid in which the player undertakes to win no tricks

explanation.surface: Someone vows they are being straight.
explanation.walkthrough: In solo whist this bid undertakes to take no tricks at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-game declaration undertaking to lose every trick.

clue.text: Shipping company after vessel for medicinal ointment

indicators.note: after puts the shipping company piece behind the vessel

parts.note: a vase is a vessel
a line is a shipping company

explanation.surface: A shipping firm follows a ship with medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaseline is a trademarked petroleum jelly used as a soothing ointment.

clue.text: Bill's teacher

definitions.meaning: British slang for a schoolmaster or magistrate

explanation.surface: Bill is a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's bill; also old British schoolboy slang for a schoolmaster.

clue.text: Work for the enemy, as a prisoner might do

definitions.text: Work for the enemy, as a prisoner might do

parts.words: Work for the enemy, as a prisoner might do
parts.note: suggests collaborating, but the enemy is time itself, and a prisoner works off a sentence

explanation.surface: A captive is made to collaborate with the foe.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo a prison sentence; time is proverbially the enemy.
